about: Whether a source says a fish species' young look clearly different from its adult, the juvenile card's trigger (docs/decisions/2026-11-20-juvenile-card-shows-young-beside-adult.md): differs true, a source says the juveniles look clearly different (colour or pattern, not a matter of degree nor of shape alone); false, a source says they look like the adult (or like one adult sex or phase); sub true, a source names a sub-adult stage with its own look, false, a source gives sub-adults the juvenile's or the adult's look. Each value with its sources {t, u}, the quote q (the sources' words, ' | ' between quotes), note (why, in our words) and the date read. unknown: species read with no source either way (no card). Built into fish.json species jd {d, sub, src, ssrc} by tools/build_fish.py (juv_differs); the juvenile card (quiz.js juvCard) reads differs alone, for juveniles and sub-adults alike (sub is information only); the draw, the ease and the judging never read it. Sources that disagree are in points.json (rule C5), never settled here.

Acanthurus olivaceus.q: Body of adult dark grayish brown; juveniles yellow; posterior to upper end of gill opening is a bright orange horizontal band, with purplish black border. | The bright yellow juveniles have a pale blue margin on the anal fin, and the band behind the eye gradually develops with growth.

Acanthurus pyroferus.q: A yellowish-brown surgeonfish with a white band around the mouth, an orange to black margin around the eye, a dark band from the chin to the top of the gill cover, an orange area around the pectoral fin base, and a yellow margin on the caudal fin. The yellow juveniles mimic several species of pygmy angelfish of the genus Centropyge

Aluterus scriptus.q: olive brown to grey in color, juveniles may be yellowish brown with dark spots
Aluterus scriptus.note: the juvenile 'may be' yellowish brown with dark spots

Amphiprion biaculeatus.q: Male and juvenile fish are bright red-orange which darkens on the fish changing to female, ranging from maroon to dark brown.

Anampses caeruleopunctatus.q: Very small juveniles are a mottled olive-green with narrow brown stripes and a mostly transparent tail. | Juveniles have a broad transparent margin on the caudal fin which lacks the pale blue spots of females.

Anampses melanurus.q: The primary phase of this species closely resembles that of A. meleagrides , but never has a uniformly yellow tail, and the color pattern does not change much with growth or sex

Anyperodon leucogrammicus.q: A slender greenish to brownish-grey rockcod with reddish spots, 3-4 irregular pale stripes along the sides, and a pointed snout. The distinctive blue and gold striped juveniles mimic some small lined wrasses of the genus Halichoeres

Arothron stellatus.q: Juveniles are orange with dark stripes that break up into spots as they grow. | Juveniles with dark stripes on belly, becoming spots with growth

Bodianus axillaris.q: Juveniles and females easily recognized by the generally black body with large white spots | Females and juveniles are blackish overall with large white spots along the upper and lower sides.
Bodianus axillaris.note: like the females; males differ (Fishes of Australia re-read 2026-11-20: males reddish-brown in front, white behind)

Bodianus mesothorax.q: Color of juveniles changes completely to adult pattern when about 5-6 cm long. | Juveniles are deep purple with two rows of bright yellow spots.

Canthigaster valentini.q: In all cases, except for C. amboinensis and C. callisterna, the juveniles (individuals less than approximately 35 mm SL) resemble the adults, although the number of spots or stripes may be reduced.

Caranx melampygus.q: covered with small blue black spots (forming at about 16 to 22 cm fork length and increasing in number with size); second dorsal, anal, and caudal fins electric blue; juveniles and young adults, head and body silvery grey and fins pale to dark dusky, except pectoral fins yellow

Caranx sexfasciatus.q: A large dark bluish-green to gold trevally, a paler yellowish-green to silvery below, with a dark caudal fin and dark grey to dusky tips on the soft dorsal and anal fins. Juveniles have 4-7 broad dark cross-bars, a round dark spot on the gill cover and a yellow caudal fin with black tip on the upper lobe.

Centropyge bicolor.q: Adults and juveniles with similar colouration.

Cephalopholis boenak.q: A brownish to greenish-grey rockcod, usually with 7-8 dark bars on sides, a broad dark submarginal band and a narrow white margin on the dorsal, anal fins, and upper and lower caudal-fin lobes. Juveniles are yellowish on the rear of the body with a white stripe from the snout to the origin of the dorsal fin.

Cephalopholis cyanostigma.q: Juveniles dark brown with bright yellow dorsal, anal, pelvic and tail fins. | At size about 9 cm, small scattered blue dots appear and yellow on fins begins to recede

Cephalopholis miniata.q: Color orange-red to reddish brown, usually dark posteriorly with numerous bright blue spots | juveniles may be yellow with scattered faint blue spots.

Cephalopholis sonnerati.q: Adults from Pacific Ocean generally pale reddish to yellowish brown, covered with numerous small brownish red or dark brown spots on head, body, and fins; while the juveniles are dark reddish brown to nearly black, the rear margin of caudal fin and sometimes pectoral fins whitish

Cetoscarus ocellatus.q: Juveniles are usually white with a thick orange band that surrounds the head, except snout and chin. | Females of the initial phase have a dark purple to reddish brown head, finely spotted with black ventrally. | The color of the C. ocellatus varies between genders as well as between adults and juveniles.

Cheilinus fasciatus.q: Colour of subadults and females with similar white bars on nape and body as juveniles
Cheilinus fasciatus.sub_q: Colour of subadults and females with similar white bars on nape and body as juveniles

Chlorurus spilurus.q: Females (initial phase) are dark brownish-maroon with a pinkish/red snout and chin, and often two rows of white spots along the side. | Small juveniles are dark brown with four white stripes along the side.
Chlorurus spilurus.sub_q: Small juveniles are dark brown with four white stripes along the side. | Larger juveniles gradually brownish-maroon anteriorly with a white tail and a white caudal peduncles surrounding a large dark spot.
Chlorurus spilurus.sub_note: small striped juveniles, then larger maroon-and-white-tail juveniles

Coris batuensis.q: Body overall pale greenish to whitish with several dark bars on upper sides; A black ocellus in middle of dorsal fin (lost in large males) and a black marking at pectoral-fin base; Juveniles greenish (whitish anteriorly) with pink to reddish spots and several ocelli on dorsal fin.

Coris gaimard.q: As a juvenile, it is a bright red colour with large, black-margined white spots. | As an adult, it has a pink face and fins, with the exception of the tail fin, which is bright yellow. | The body is green towards the anterior darkening and decorated with bright blue specks towards the caudal peduncle.

Ctenochaetus binotatus.q: Caudal fin brown in adults, yellow in young.

Ctenochaetus cyanocheilus.q: Color orangish brown to dark brown with bluish lines following scale rows | Young bright yellow.

Cyclichthys orbicularis.q: Adults brown to grey with blotches and clusters of black spots on back and sides; pelagic juveniles covered with black spots

Dascyllus aruanus.q: The colors remain the same throughout their lives.

Dascyllus trimaculatus.q: Juveniles are black often with bluish scale centres, and have a white blotch on the forehead and another on the upper side. | Adults lack the spot on the head, and the spot on the sides becomes smaller and disappears with age.
Dascyllus trimaculatus.note: the juvenile's white spots shrink or go; partly a difference of degree

Diagramma melanacrum.q: Juveniles and subadults are yellowish with black stripes and rows of large spots along the sides. | Silvery-grey to yellowish sweetlip with brown spots on the head and body
Diagramma melanacrum.sub_q: Juveniles and subadults are yellowish with black stripes and rows of large spots along the sides.
Diagramma melanacrum.sub_note: the source gives subadults the juvenile's pattern, not a separate one

Diagramma pictum.q: Colour: Adults light grey with scattered large blackish blotches on sides, white on belly. Juveniles with conspicuous alternating black and white stripes, and yellowish on head and belly. Stripes eventually break up into spots that disappear in adults.
Diagramma pictum.sub_q: Stripes eventually break up into spots that disappear in adults. | Adults are slate-grey, and along with subadult fish, lack yellow or orange spots
Diagramma pictum.sub_note: a spotted stage between the striped juvenile and the adult; the adult's own spotting varies by region (Fishes of Australia: Australian adults and subadults slate-grey without yellow or orange spots), not settled here

Diodon holocanthus.q: Pelagic juveniles with spots, particularly prominent on belly; adults with dark blotches across back and spots between the blotches; fins without spots

Diploprion bifasciatum.q: Normally yellow, but sometimes nearly all black and juveniles take-on colors of the local venomous Meiacanthus blennies that are yellow or grey | Small juveniles are bluish on the front half of the body becoming yellow towards the rear, with a black spinous dorsal fin.

Diproctacanthus xanthurus.q: Juveniles with 3 broad black stripes from head to caudal fin where the stripes merge; with growth, lower stripe disappears, upper stripe is less distinct; black caudal fin becomes entirely yellow in adults.

Dischistodus perspicillatus.q: Light body and fins, with 3 black patches on upper body in adult, 2 black bars in juvenile.

Epinephelus maculatus.q: Small juveniles are black with white blotches, becoming more spotted with age.

Gnathanodon speciosus.q: Adults are silvery grey, with black spots or blotches scattered on sides, and often faint bands. | Juveniles and subadults are bright yellow with narrow blackish bars on head and sides, the first through the eye.
Gnathanodon speciosus.sub_q: Juveniles and subadults are bright yellow with narrow blackish bars on head and sides, the first through the eye.

Gracila albomarginata.q: The juveniles are colourful being violet with bright red margins on their dorsal, anal and caudal fins. | a greenish to reddish-brown or brownish-grey body

Grammistes sexlineatus.q: small juveniles with spots, specimens up to 5 cm SL with 3 stripes, specimens at least 8 cm SL with 6 stripes, the number of stripes increases and may break into a series of dashes in large adults | Small juveniles have only two white stripes, dividing with growth into numerous lines.

Halichoeres chloropterus.q: Juveniles and females with dark dots dorsally and posteriorly

Halichoeres hortulanus.q: Small juveniles black and white, gradually changing with growth to adult pattern

Halichoeres margaritaceus.q: One of several similar species that have near identical juvenile and female stages

Halichoeres melanurus.q: Females and juveniles with fine pinstripes, two ocelli on dorsal fin (which disappear with age), and one on upper tail base.

Halichoeres prosopeion.q: Adult Twotone Wrasse are blue on the front half of the body, changing abruptly to yellow posteriorly. | Juvenile Twotone Wrasse are white with four black stripes on the body.

Halichoeres richmondi.q: Females and juveniles with yellow and blue stripes along body similar to H. melanurus (Hoeven's Wrasse) , best distinguished by presence of males.

Hemigymnus fasciatus.q: Juveniles are dark brown with six narrow irregular white bars, the first across the nape and chest, the next three extending onto the dorsal and anal fins, and the last two on the caudal peduncle and caudal-fin base; head with pale yellowish lines radiating from eye, lips whitish. | Females are blackish with four white bars, the first progressively broader ventrally, ending on abdomen, the remaining bars progressively thinner, the last two sometimes faint

Hippocampus kuda.q: Juvenile seahorses emerge from the pouch as independent, miniature adults.
Hippocampus kuda.note: shape: miniature adults with other proportions

Hipposcarus longiceps.q: Females (initial phase) are pale brown to pale grey with a yellowish tail. Small juveniles are whitish to pale brownish with a broad orange stripe ending in a black spot on the tail base.

Hologymnosus doliatus.q: Juveniles whitish with three narrow orange-red stripes. | Initial phase pale bluish, greenish or pinkish gray with 20-23 orange brown bars on body

Iniistius aneitensis.q: Juveniles light with brown blotches and two false eye spots on the dorsal fin, adults gray with large white patch behind the pectoral fins and three dark vertical blotches

Labrichthys unilineatus.q: juveniles brown with 2 bluish white stripes on body, the lateral stripe disappearing with increase in size; female yellowish brown, stripes dull and faint

Labroides bicolor.q: The male is black with light color in the back of the body | the female is gray with black | juveniles are yellow and black | Juveniles white or pale yellow with black stripe from snout through eye which terminates two thirds of the way along body.

Labroides dimidiatus.q: The young are black with an electric-blue line. | the back and the stomach are white (sometimes slightly yellowish) | This white part changes to a bright blue on the front of the animal, while the black band widens at the tail.

Labropsis manabei.q: juveniles and small females with 3 broad black stripes on head and body, separated by narrow pale blue stripes.
Labropsis manabei.note: like the small females; larger adults change colour

Lethrinus erythracanthus.q: A large dark grey emperor with a greyish-blue head and yellow to yellowish-orange fins. Juveniles are yellowish with a grey head and narrow whitish broken lines or stripes along the sides.

Lutjanus argentimaculatus.q: Juveniles have a series of about 8 whitish bars on the sides, and 1-2 blue lines across the cheek. | Colour of the body generally greenish brown on back, grading to reddish

Lutjanus lemniscatus.q: Juveniles are pale grey with a broad black mid-lateral stripe between narrow white stripes from the tip of the snout to the tail base. | A greyish to pinkish-brown, to olive-green or silvery tropical snapper with dusky brown to blackish dorsal and caudal fins (often with a narrow white margin).

Lutjanus russellii.q: Juveniles (usually <5 cm SL) are white with four (sometimes broken) brown to blackish stripes along the side, and a horizontally-elongate black spot or ocellus on the lateral line. | Colour generally pink to whitish with a silvery sheen; a black spot, mainly above lateral line, below anterior rays of soft dorsal fin

Lutjanus sebae.q: Juveniles and young adults have a dark red band from the snout tip through the eye to the first dorsal-fin spine, a broad band from the middle of the dorsal-fin spines to the pelvic fin, and a diagonal band from the end of the last dorsal spine to the lower lobe of the caudal fin. | Large adults become uniformly red

Lutjanus vitta.sub_q: Juveniles and sub-adults have a broader, darker stripe than adults. | Juveniles and sub-adults with an intensely black mid-lateral stripe and an oval black spot, eye-sized or greater, lying in the middle of the stripe below last dorsal spines.

Macolor macularis.q: juveniles with distinct black and white pattern, with more than 5 white spots on back | Colour of adults dark grey brown dorsally and shading to yellow on head and ventral body, head with fine blue lines or spots

Macolor niger.q: juveniles with black and white pattern but broader white area encompassing posterior head and adjacent body and with less than 5 white spots on back | Colour of adults silvery grey, strongly blotched with blackish patches

Macropharyngodon meleagris.q: Color in life of young and females whitish to greenish with irregular black spots

Macropharyngodon negrosensis.q: Females and juveniles usually seen, and have a dense covering of fine white spots on black body, white dorsal fin crossed by black lines, black ventral and anal fins, transparent tail fin.

Monotaxis grandoculis.q: Juveniles have 3 broad dark brown to blackish bars or saddles on the body (rear two extending onto dorsal fin), a black bar through the eye and an orange to reddish band along the outer caudal-fin lobes. | Color of adult silvery grey with narrow dark scale margins, lips yellowish, a large black blotch covering pectoral fin axil

Naso brevirostris.sub_q: Subadults have small dark spots on the head and body, and the horn starts as a bump in juveniles from a length of about 10 cm.

Naso vlamingii.q: Juveniles olive-brown with a covering of blue spots and dashes. | Head profile with rounded nose-like bump above mouth, blue or violet stripe across snout between eyes, narrow bars on body which break in to spots on upper body and underside, blue lips, and a large blue or violet patch behind gill cover over pectoral fin base.

Neoglyphidodon melas.q: Adults are a deep bluish-black, and the juveniles are very pale blue with a yellow dorsal surface, yellow outer caudal-fin rays

Neoglyphidodon nigroris.q: juveniles distinctively yellow with two black stripes | Juveniles are bright yellow with a pair of black stripes along the head and body, and a black spot at the pectoral-fin base.

Neoglyphidodon thoracotaeniatus.q: Small juveniles bright yellow with black band, gradually changes to an all black posterior body when adult
Neoglyphidodon thoracotaeniatus.sub_q: Small juveniles bright yellow with black band, gradually changes to an all black posterior body when adult | Juveniles dark posteriorly with large black ocellus at mid-base of dorsal fin
Neoglyphidodon thoracotaeniatus.sub_note: yellow small juvenile, then a dark-rear juvenile with a dorsal ocellus

Novaculichthys taeniourus.q: Juveniles found in Hawaii are usually green and those in the western Pacific are burgundy to brownish. | Both are spotted in white. | The adult fish has a dark greenish-brown body with an elongated white spot on each scale.
Novaculichthys taeniourus.note: the article's juvenile colour sentence is marked 'citation needed'

Novaculoides macrolepidotus.q: Adults are usually bright green, while juveniles are variable in colour ranging from brown to green, usually with a blotched pattern.
Novaculoides macrolepidotus.sub_q: Juvenile and subadult Seagrass Wrasses mimic venomous waspfishes of the genus Ablaby s.

Oplopomus oplopomus.sub_q: subadults lack the blue and yellow spotting but have more black spots
Oplopomus oplopomus.sub_note: subadults lack the adult's blue and yellow spots

Ostorhinchus aureus.q: Black bar encircling caudal peduncle present in both young and adult phases

Ostorhinchus compressus.q: Juveniles have yellow tail base where the mid stripe ends in black spot, stripes are black rather than brown and appear more even, and body shape is more like a normal cardinalfish shape.

Ostracion cubicus.q: Juveniles bright yellow with black spots; the spots decrease proportionately and the bright yellow becomes a dirty mustard with growth; large adults become bluish with yellowish seams between the plates.

Ostracion meleagris.q: Juveniles and females brown or green with white spots; large males with orange bands and spots on side of body

Oxycheilinus bimaculatus.q: Juveniles have a broad, dark mid-lateral stripe that breaks into dark blotches in adults, the largest above the pectoral-fin tip. | Young with a broad, dark lateral stripe which breaks into dark blotches in adults

Paracirrhites forsteri.q: In Oceania, juveniles are a golden green dorsally and white ventrally; in continental areas juveniles may be red dorsally | Body yellowish with broad blackish stripe on upper side; head and anterior part of body with small dark reddish spots | Color changes with growth as well as varies among adults

Parupeneus heptacantha.sub_q: an indistinct narrow yellow stripe often visible above the lateral line (more evident in juveniles and subadults)
Parupeneus heptacantha.sub_note: the stripe is clearer in juveniles and subadults alike

Pholidichthys leucotaenia.q: Juveniles resemble the venomous striped catfish Plotosus lineatus . | Adults live secretively in reefs and have a barred or spotted color pattern

Platax batavianus.q: Juveniles and adults have different coloration. | Adults are silver with a dark bar around the eye and a faint one on the back. | Juveniles are brown and are tall in appearance.
Platax batavianus.sub_q: Small juveniles black, vertical white lines on body and fins. | Subadults brown, with black bar from nape, over eye to chest and another black bar from dorsal-fin origin, over pectoral fins to pelvic fins, pectoral and pelvic fins dark brown or black.
Platax batavianus.sub_note: black-and-white small juvenile, then a brown subadult with black bars, then the silver adult

Platax boersii.q: Small juveniles yellowish brown or silvery, with 2 black bars as in adults.

Platax orbicularis.q: The colour of adults is silvery grey with black vertical bars running through the pectoral fin and eye. | The small juveniles are reddish brown in colour, marked with irregular black spots and blotches

Platax pinnatus.q: The juveniles are mainly black with the body and median fins outlined in orange | The overall colour is silvery with a dusky or dark vertical bar running through the eye.

Platax teira.q: Very small juveniles are brownish and resemble floating leaves. | Yellowish silvery or dusky, with a black (or dusky) bar through eye and another dark bar from dorsal-fin origin across rear edge of operculum and pectoral-fin base to belly
Platax teira.note: Wikipedia (read 2026-11-20) gives the adult as 'usually silver, grey or brownish', overlapping the brownish juvenile

Plectorhinchus chaetodonoides.q: juveniles brownish with large, well-defined creamy white blotches on body that include brown spots with age; gradually becoming greyish with large, deep brown spots.
Plectorhinchus chaetodonoides.sub_q: juveniles brownish with large, well-defined creamy white blotches on body that include brown spots with age; gradually becoming greyish with large, deep brown spots.
Plectorhinchus chaetodonoides.sub_note: white blotches that come to include brown spots, then grey with brown spots

Plectorhinchus lessonii.q: Juveniles are black with white horizontal stripes. | They change appearance as they mature reaching 30 cm in length.
Plectorhinchus lessonii.note: the sources disagree on the adult's pattern (points.json fish-juv-plectorhinchus-lessonii), not on the change

Plectorhinchus lineatus.q: Colour of juveniles with few horizontal to slightly oblique dark brown bands which subdivide with age until the body appears to be dark chocolate brown above, with a network of fine white lines running up and back
Plectorhinchus lineatus.sub_q: Juveniles and subadult fish have black horizontal stripes along the body that become increasingly diagonal with growth.
Plectorhinchus lineatus.sub_note: subadults share the juvenile stripes, which turn diagonal gradually

Plectorhinchus picus.q: The Dotted Sweetlips is white to grey with numerous small black spots on the upper half of the head and body. | Juveniles are black above and white below. | They have a white snout, a white saddle on the nape and another on the back below the middle of the dorsal fin.

Plectorhinchus vittatus.q: juveniles with connected black blotches and spots that gradually break up into horizontal stripes; pectoral fins black in juveniles becoming uniform yellow in adults

Pomacanthus imperator.q: The emperor angelfish shows a marked difference between the juveniles and the adults. | The juveniles have a dark blue body which is marked with concentric curving lines | The adults are striped with blue and yellow horizontal stripes

Pomacanthus navarchus.q: Juvenile fish are dark blue with slightly curved, white lateral stripes. | Adult fish have three main colored sections
Pomacanthus navarchus.sub_q: The change from the juvenile to the adult coloring takes place quite abruptly, with little intermediate coloring.
Pomacanthus navarchus.sub_note: the change is abrupt, little intermediate colouring

Pomacanthus semicirculatus.q: The adults are brownish green in colour with the scales edged in blue creating a blue speckling over the body and tail. | The juveniles in contrast, are blue-black marked from top to bottom with narrow white stripes. | The juveniles gradually adopt the adult colouration when they are 8 to 16 centimetres (3.1 to 6.3 in).

Pomacanthus sexstriatus.q: juveniles have an overall blue-black color broken by many vertical white bands | The adults, in contrast, have an overall color of brownish-yellow on the body and the median fins, with vivid blue spots.

Pseudanthias huchtii.q: Juveniles same colouration as females but with green eyes.

Pseudodax moluccanus.sub_q: Juveniles are pale blue with a broad midbody stripe, and subadults have a yellow band on the tail base.
Pseudodax moluccanus.sub_note: subadults gain a yellow tail-base band

Pygoplites diacanthus.q: Juveniles (not shown) with similar markings to adults.
Pygoplites diacanthus.note: Fishes of Australia (as read 2026-11-19) adds fewer bands, a dorsal ocellus and no eye patch (degree)

Rhinomuraena quaesita.q: Juveniles all black, males have yellow dorsal fin and females change to a nearly all yellow color, but usually with blue in the posterior | Males are bright blue with a yellow snout, lower jaw and dorsal fin.
Rhinomuraena quaesita.sub_q: Juveniles and subadults are jet black with a yellow dorsal fin.
Rhinomuraena quaesita.sub_note: subadults share the black juvenile colour

Scarus altipinnis.q: Females (initial phase) area brownish with scattered white spots, and small juveniles have a striped to mottled body with a distinctive yellow head.

Scarus niger.q: Females have a reddish head, belly and fins, with wavy dark and white stripes along the side, dark green bands around the mouth and eye. | Juveniles are dark greenish black, covered in small white spots, with a black spot at the top and bottom of a white band on the tail base.

Scarus oviceps.q: S. oviceps juvenile and female have single light bar on upper side.

Scolopsis affinis.q: Juveniles with dusky brown stripe on either side of dorsal midline, and dusky brown midlateral stripe, yellowish above anteriorly. | Color: Body silvery-white.

Scolopsis bilineata.q: juveniles with alternating black and yellow stripes on the upper half and whitish below, Batesian mimic of the poison-fanged blenny Meiacanthus grammistes | Colour dark grey on head and back with diagonal black-edged white band separating dark area from the rest of the mainly whitish body; white blotch below posterior dorsal fin

Scolopsis lineata.q: Upper body olive brown, silvery-white below. 3 yellowish white stripes along head and body. Juveniles white, with 3 black bands on upper half of body, interspace between lower pair of yellow bands; black spot between first three dorsal spines.

Seriola dumerili.q: Small juveniles have clear fins and a series of bands along the body that often appear divided. | A large predatory jack with a brownish to bluish-grey body becoming silvery-white below, a dusky to dark stripe from the snout to just before the dorsal fin, and a dusky band from the upper jaw through the eye to the first dorsal fin.

Siganus corallinus.q: Small juveniles have narrow blue vertical lines on the sides that fragment into ocelli with growth. | Very small juveniles (up to 50 mm SL) may have vertical blue lines on side, fragmenting into the ocelli with increase in size.

Sufflamen bursa.sub_q: The characteristic scythe mark crossing the pectoral base is yellowish-tan to green in juveniles and subadults.

Taeniura lymma.q: Females bear litters of up to seven young, each a miniature version of the adult measuring around 13–14 cm (5.1–5.5 in) across.

Variola albimarginata.q: juveniles similar in colour to adults, but with relatively fewer and larger pale blue or pink spots
